positions.as_written: Take the history: the rest pain, the night pain, the walking distance, the stairs, and what the patient has stopped doing.
Assess the alignment standing from the front and from the side, recording varus, valgus and any fixed flexion.
Measure the range, recording the fixed flexion deficit first and the flexion second, since the deficit is the one that limits function.
Assess the collateral ligaments, because the worn compartment shortens its own side and the opposite ligament may have stretched.
Assess the patellofemoral joint, since it is involved in a large proportion of worn knees and is often not examined.
